name: AFCAT
approxCandidates: ≈2–3 lakh applicants per cycle (approx.); about 250–350 vacancies per cycle
eligibility: Graduate (B.E./B.Tech for Technical); 20–24 yrs for Flying branch, 20–26 yrs for Ground Duty branches

notification.summary: AFCAT 02/2026 was held on 8 August 2026, and the result was declared on 9 September 2026. AFCAT 01/2027 is expected to be notified in early-to-mid November 2026 (estimated from the previous cycle), with applications in November–December 2026 and the exam around late January to February 2027. Nothing has been confirmed on afcat.cdac.in yet.

pattern.notes: Section counts are the usual split (GA 20–25, English 30, Numerical 18–20, Reasoning 25–27) and vary slightly from cycle to cycle. There is no sectional time limit. Ground Duty (Technical) applicants also take the Engineering Knowledge Test (50 questions, 150 marks, 45 minutes), which is not simulated. The bank leaves out the figure-based spatial items in Reasoning & Military Aptitude because they cannot be shown as text.

trendAnalysis.summary: The paper is moderate overall and speed matters, with 100 questions in 120 minutes and −1 per wrong answer. English (30 questions) is the highest-scoring area: synonyms, antonyms, idioms, error detection, completion and one passage. General Awareness leans on defence and aviation, static history and geography, and recent events (awards, sports, exercises). Numerical Ability stays at arithmetic level (percentages, speed–distance, ratios, interest) with simple calculations. Reasoning & Military Aptitude has many figure-based items (pattern completion, embedded and mirror images, dot situations) along with verbal analogy, series and coding. Difficulty and section mix have been stable over 2024–26.

resources.notes: The IAF does not officially publish past AFCAT papers. The AFCAT candidate portal (afcat.cdac.in) offers an online practice test and the syllabus, and provisional answer keys are shown to candidates there after each exam. Circulating 'previous papers' are memory-based.

pyqBlueprint.method: The IAF does not publish AFCAT papers, so the patterns come from candidate-feedback analyses of the 2024, 2025 and 2026 shifts (Physics Wallah 22/23 Feb 2025 and 31 Jan 2026, PracticeMock, Careers360, Studyriserr). For example, the 22 Feb 2025 shift had GA 25 / English 30 / Numerical 20 / Reasoning 25, with about 7 current-affairs and 6 geography GA items and 3 each of coding-decoding and odd-one-out. Item-level details are from memory-based reconstructions and the writer's own knowledge, since full pages could not be fetched. Figure-based spatial items are represented only by their text-renderable variants (painted-cube counting, mirror-image clock).

archetypes.pattern: Ancient/medieval battles, dynasties and founders (Haldighati, Talikota, Maurya founder): one-line fact recall.
Modern history: dates and slogans of freedom-struggle events (Jallianwala Bagh, Quit India).
Indian geography: lakes, rivers, national parks and their states.
World geography: straits, deserts and waterbodies separating land masses.
Constitutional articles, schedules, oaths and the election of constitutional functionaries.
Economic institutions and their roles (NABARD, NSO, RBI).
Physics behind flight and instruments (barometer, Bernoulli lift, Mach number).
Everyday chemistry and biology facts (gases in use, vitamins, human body).
IAF organisation and facts: Air Force Day, motto, commands and their headquarters.
Aircraft, missiles and their manufacturers/origin (Tejas, Rafale, BrahMos).
Bilateral and multilateral air/military exercises and partner countries (Garuda, Red Flag, Cope India).
Dance forms, temples and monuments with their state or builder.
Trophies/cups and sports, national sports awards and their purpose.
Choose the synonym of a single word (diligent, candid, lucid).
Choose the antonym of a single word; a synonym is planted among the options.
Find the erroneous part: subject–verb agreement ('one of', 'every', 'news').
Find the erroneous part: preposition or tense misuse ('since five years', 'married with', past time with present perfect).
Fill the blank with the right preposition or phrasal-verb particle (take off, look into, call off).
Fill the blank with the correct tense/conditional or auxiliary (had, would have).
Meaning of a common idiom; distractors are literal readings.
One passage (often on aviation/science) with factual and author's-view questions.
Cloze passage/sentence: choose the word that fits the blank.
Percentage basics: x% of y% of z, 'by how much less', successive change, pass/fail overlap.
Profit/loss per cent and marked price–discount–gain combinations.
Dividing a sum in a ratio, or converting equal products (3A = 4B = 6C) to a ratio.
Average with one item added or removed (instructor/captain age, removed number).
SI/CI: interest amount, rate when a sum doubles, 2-year CI.
Men–days proportion or finding one worker's time from joint and individual times.
Unit conversion, average speed for a round trip, trains crossing poles or each other.
Decimal simplification using identities (a² − b²)/(a − b) or ×/÷ of decimals.
LCM/HCF and divisibility: smallest/largest number divisible by given numbers.
Word analogy based on function/instrument–measure/worker–tool.
Number or letter-group analogy (n : n³, letter shifts).
Odd one out among words, aircraft/weapons or numbers (prime/square property).
Number series: n² + n, ×2 + 1, differences doubling, nⁿ.
Letter series with fixed gaps or paired forward/backward letters.
Letter-shift coding (+1/−1 for each letter).
Number coding from alphabet positions (position values, sum × k).
Direction sense: walk-and-turn path, final distance and direction.
Blood relations from a statement or chain of relations.
Rank in a row from left/right ends.
Linear or circular seating with 4–6 people and 3–4 clues.
Painted-cube cutting: count small cubes with 0/1/2/3 faces painted.
Mirror/water images, including the mirror image of a clock time.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the question.
'The first powered, controlled aeroplane flight by the Wright brothers in 1903 lasted only about twelve seconds. Yet that brief hop changed the course of history. Within a few decades aircraft were crossing oceans, and air power had become decisive in war. What made the Wrights succeed where others had failed was not a more powerful engine but their careful attention to control: they understood that an aircraft must be steered and balanced in the air, and they solved this problem through patient experiment.'
According to the passage, the main reason for the Wright brothers' success was:
options: Careful attention to controlling and balancing the aircraft
questions.explanation: The passage says success came 'not [from] a more powerful engine but their careful attention to control'.

relevance.note: Aviation RC (Wright brothers) with factual reason Q matches AFCAT E08

questions.question: A's salary is 25% more than B's. By what percentage is B's salary less than A's?

questions.question: Five aircraft P, Q, R, S and T are parked in a row. R is at the extreme left and S is at the extreme right. P is immediately to the left of Q, and T is next to R. Which aircraft is in the middle?
questions.explanation: R occupies position 1 and S position 5. T is next to R, so T is at 2, leaving P at 3 and Q at 4. The order is R T P Q S, so P is in the middle.

questions.question:
Read the passage and answer the question.
'Unmanned aerial vehicles, commonly called drones, were first developed mainly for military surveillance. Today they are increasingly used in disaster relief. After floods or earthquakes, roads are often blocked, and helicopters may be unavailable or too costly to deploy for every small task. Drones can quickly survey damaged areas, locate stranded people with thermal cameras and even deliver light packages of medicine. Their limited payload and battery life, however, mean that they support rather than replace conventional rescue teams.'
According to the passage, drones are useful after disasters because they:
options: were originally designed for disaster relief
can quickly survey areas when roads are blocked
questions.explanation: The passage says drones can quickly survey damaged areas when roads are blocked. It mentions their limited payload and battery life, and says they were first built for military surveillance.

relevance.note: Drone RC factual Q is aviation-themed AFCAT style
